findings.description: The four 'core.worktree elsewhere' tests can't catch a revert of their fixes. `safeArgv` (src/core/git-diff.client.ts:737-744) already passes `--work-tree=<repo>` on every gate spawn, which overrides `core.worktree`, so the tests still pass with `--full-tree`, `:(top,...)`, `--no-relative` and `-c diff.relative=false` removed. They would only start covering those flags if `safeArgv` stopped pinning the work tree; for now, either rewrite them or label them as defence in depth.
ADR 0139 says the full test stage fails 'in nine cases', but the list after it now has more than nine entries. Drop the number or recount it.

One line of the `changesOnlyUntested` JSDoc runs to about 130 characters, against the roughly 80-column wrapping used in the rest of the file. Rewrap it after 'so the skip holds only if both readings are listed,'.

`listed` is checked twice: `changedPaths.every(listed)` runs first, then `checked.every(listed)` runs over a superset of the same paths. Keep the first check only if the early exit before the git call is intended, and say so in a short comment.

`measureBranch` now runs `rawDiffEntries(repoPath, targetSha, sha)` just to collect rename sources, and `changesOnlyUntested` then runs the same `--raw -M` diff of the same pair again. Computing the entries once and passing them in would save a git subprocess.

Rename sources now go through `foldsOntoAnother`, so a rename that only changes the case of a listed doc (docs/Guide.md -> docs/guide.md) runs the full suite where it used to skip it. This is over-cautious rather than unsafe, since both spellings are on the list.

The PR rewrites the landed text of ADR 0139 in place ('six cases' becomes 'nine', the rename bullet and test-scan paragraph are reworded). docs/adr/README.md says a landed decision gets a dated amendment section or a new decision linked through `Amends:`. Ignore this if #287's version of 0139 never landed.

process_issues.description: The correctness reviewer tagged the vacuous-test finding important, and the validator confirmed it. The orchestrator downgraded it to nit: the validator found no failure the gate can reach today, because safeArgv's --work-tree pin defeats the core.worktree attack in production too.

Dropped three minor findings that didn't clear the bar: a low-confidence suggestion to drop the Set dedup, a suggestion to revert the listedFiles temp-tree test (the author gave a reason for that change), and a low-confidence docs nit on a test JSDoc clause.

Skipped review-context, review-maintainability, review-workflow-safety and review-spec: the PR changes no infra or workflow surfaces and cites no spec source. Standard depth leaves maintainability out.
